The physical reorder itself is clean: all 16 tables are present in docs/appendix3_utility.md in strict numeric order S1 to S16, every caption maps to the content the old-to-new map predicts, and a block-by-block comparison against work_notes/pre_reorder shows that no table lost or swapped its note paragraph, its rows, or its lettered footnotes. The four newly added citations (S4 at manuscript line 107, S9 at 158, S13 at 166, S15 at 182) all sit in sentences where those tables genuinely belong.

The renumbering did not land. There is a systematic bug: every multi-table reference that was written as a RANGE or a LIST in the source had the old-to-new map applied a second time (and in one case a third time), while single-table references were mapped exactly once and are correct. Seven such references now point at the wrong tables - four in the manuscript body (lines 158, 166, 169, 182), two in docs/appendix3_utility.md (lines 3 and 232), one in docs/appendix4_ceiling.md (line 3). Each is reconstructible: {S11,S12} became {S2,S11} instead of {S9,S11}, {S1,S2,S3} became {S13,S1,S7} instead of {S4,S5,S15}, {S5,S10} became the range "S13 to S14" instead of the list "S6 and S7", and so on. Every single-table reference I checked across all nine documents - 40 of them - resolves correctly to a table whose content matches the citing sentence.

Two positional statements went stale with the move: "Table S16 above" now points downward, and "Table S3, placed last so that the appendix tables run in numerical order" describes a layout that no longer exists. docs/appendix4_ceiling.md otherwise contains no sentence implying a table is nearby.

Fourteen findings, seven of them blocking. I did not report the duplicated sentence at manuscript line 105 or the duplicated abbreviation footnotes in appendix3, both of which predate this delta (present identically in work_notes/pre_restructure).
